$comment: Approximate viewpoint centroids, applied to rows by id in
src/proposal-spots-data.ts. Golden hour is computed from these, and it is
half of what engagedmoon sells, so the provenance of every pair matters
more than the count.
WHERE THESE CAME FROM. All nine were already in production, in
engagedmoon's own copy of this dataset (~/engagedmoon/src/lib/
proposal-spots.ts), computing live sunset windows. They are MOVED here,
not derived: shared-data is the canonical home now, and leaving them in
the fork is how the two copies drift. Each was matched to a shared-data
row only where the two rows name the SAME PLACE — never by city, never by
proximity.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT MATCHED. engagedmoon has 14 rows with
coordinates; 5 of them have no same-place row here and are omitted rather
than attached to a neighbour:
- sand-harbor (Lake Tahoe NV) — this repo has Emerald Bay, a different
place across the lake and across a state line
- fort-zachary-taylor (Key West) — this repo has Fort Jefferson and
Mallory Square; Fort Jefferson is 70 miles west by boat
- cathedral-rock and airport-mesa (Sedona) — this repo has Bell Rock
- skyline-wilderness (Napa) — this repo has no Napa spot at all
Attaching any of those would put a real-looking coordinate on the wrong
viewpoint, which is worse than none: a spot without coordinates renders
'late afternoon' and is honest, while a spot with the wrong ones states a
clock time confidently and no reader can tell.
Central Park is the one judgement call. engagedmoon carries a single row
named 'Bethesda Terrace & Bow Bridge' with one centroid; this repo splits
them into two rows. The coordinate is Bethesda Terrace's, so it goes to
Bethesda Terrace and Bow Bridge stays without — rather than copying one
pair onto two rows a few hundred metres apart.
TO ADD MORE: do not geocode from a name. Read the authority's own map or
a published coordinate for the named viewpoint.
⚠️ ELEVATION: READ THIS BEFORE SOURCING ANOTHER SUMMIT.
engagedmoon computes sunset from these pairs assuming a FLAT SEA-LEVEL
HORIZON. It calls SunCalc.getTimes(date, lat, lng) and does not pass the
optional 4th argument, observer height in metres — see the docblock in
engagedmoon/src/lib/sunset.ts, which carries the full measurement.
For a beach or a city park that is correct. For a high viewpoint it is
not. Height-corrected vs. as-shipped, mid-June, at pairs in this file:
Dream Lake +12 min, Artist Point +12, Tramway Mountain Station +10,
Hawksbill Summit +7, Bell Rock +7 (Jordanelle measured +9 before it was
removed for an unrelated sourcing failure). The product exists to prevent
a 10–40 minute error, so those are inside the error it sells against.
It is NOT fixed by passing a height. Elevation moves sunset later; the
local terrain moves it earlier, and on a mountain the terrain usually
wins — Tramway Mountain Station's western horizon is San Jacinto Peak,
2,300 ft ABOVE the deck, so the true sunset there is probably earlier
than the flat-horizon figure, not later. A correct fix needs a terrain
horizon per spot, which nothing here has.
CONSEQUENCE FOR SOURCING: a coordinate for a summit, a ridge, an
overlook or an aerial-tram deck is a coordinate whose printed clock time
is knowably wrong by a few minutes in a direction nobody has measured.
That is a known, unresolved limitation, not a reason to withhold the
pair — but note the elevation alongside anything you add above ~1,500 m,
so whoever does fix it has the input already.
BATCH 1 (2026-08-07, revised in fix rounds 1 and 2): 16 of the 22 target
ids from .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-07-engagedmoon-coordinate-sourcing/
task-2-brief.md. Six were skipped rather than guessed — see
coordinate-sources.json's 'skipped' block for why each one has no
defensible published coordinate.
TWO of those six were fix-round REMOVALS, and they are the same mistake
twice: a coordinate for the area CONTAINING the named point, recorded as
though it were the point.
- bozeman-mt-lake-butte-overlook (round 1) — sourced to GNIS's 'Lake
Butte' Summit record, which is the mountain, not 'Lake Butte Overlook',
the constructed roadside pullout on its slope ~1 km away.
- park-city-ut-jordanelle-hailstone (round 2) — the pair was Jordanelle
State Park's whole-park coordinate from recreation.gov, on a row named
'Hailstone Overlook'. Its recorded source additionally claimed a Utah
State Parks page 'states GPS coordinates directly' when that page
publishes none, so the pair was untraceable to what was cited.
Both removals cost coverage and neither was a close call. A row with no
coordinate says 'late afternoon'; a row with the containing area's
coordinate says 8:41 PM and sounds exactly as certain as a correct one.
Where possible these are read directly from the USGS Geographic Names
Information System (GNIS) via its official public search API
(edits.nationalmap.gov/apps/gaz-domestic) — the federal authority for named
natural and cultural features, not a third-party geocoder. Where a spot is
a constructed park/building GNIS does not catalogue (it excludes most
urban parks, gardens and buildings), the coordinate is the specific
feature's published one (usually a Wikipedia infobox value), cross-checked
against the managing authority's own stated street address for that exact
site — never a city or park-district centroid.
Two are anchored to a destination in a DIFFERENT state than the
destinationId suggests — see STATE_OVERRIDE in proposal-spots-data.test.ts:
Hawksbill Summit (washington-dc-hawksbill-summit) is in Shenandoah NP, VA;
Artist Point (bozeman-mt-artist-point) is in Yellowstone, Park County, WY.
